title: Boolean Selector / Flag Arguments
pattern: Passing a boolean literal or type-unsafe selector argument to a function to direct its primary internal execution flow.
why_bad: Violates the Single Responsibility Principle. The function does more than one thing depending on the flag, and call sites become obscure (e.g., `calculate_pay(40, true)` forces the reader to look up the signature to understand what `true` means).
detection: A function signature taking a boolean parameter where the parameter is directly branched on at the top level of the function body.
counterexample: Passing boolean configurations that merely adjust an invariant property of a single task without altering the execution path of the function.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 3; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 7.5.
